name: Guinness chocolate cake
origin: A moist Irish chocolate cake using stout beer in place of some of the buttermilk a devil's-food-style batter would otherwise use; a modern classic rather than a historic recipe, popularised through Irish and British home baking in the late 20th century.

ingredients.note: cocoa fraction of a 25%-of-flour cocoa dose, split as in devils-food.json

stout is predominantly water (commercial stout is typically ~92% water by mass, the balance mostly dissolved carbohydrate and a few percent alcohol); no stout-beer substance record exists yet (see catalog.ts module notes), and the small alcohol and dissolved-solids fraction is approximated here as water for the purpose of the hydration figures, an explicitly conservative simplification

process.name: warm stout with butter and cocoa
process.description: warm stout with butter and cocoa powder until smooth

process.name: whisk in sugar and eggs
process.description: cool slightly, then whisk in sugar and eggs

process.name: fold in flour
process.description: fold in flour, leavening and salt

process.name: bake
process.description: bake in a large tin, often a springform or bundt-style pan

notes: Structurally a high-ratio chocolate cake in the same family as devils-food.json, with stout replacing buttermilk as the main liquid. Cream-cheese icing traditionally finishing this cake is a separately-prepared component, out of scope for this batter's formulation.
